newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Islamists urge quick action on corruption.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Islamists urge quick action on corruption.

text.p: The leader of a Pakistani Islamist opposition party welcomed the sacking of Benazir Bhutto's government on Tuesday, but said corrupt politicians should be brought to book before any new elections.

"We consider President Farooq Leghari's decision to dismiss the government as a welcome consitutional action," Qazi Hussain Ahmed, leader of the religious Jamaat-i-Islami party, told a news conference.
"We want the caretaker government to start a process of accountability to be conducted by the supreme judiciary of the country," the Moslem cleric said.

Jamaat-i-Islami brought several thousand supporters on to the streets of Islamabad and the nearby city of Rawalpindi last week for anti-corruption protests that provoked a heavy security response and half-paralysed the two cities for three days.
Ahmed said the whole accountability process could be completed within three months, which would allow elections to go ahead on February 3, 1997, the date set by Leghari.
"However, if elections are held without accountability, without weeding out morally corrupt people, we will agitate against this (caretaker) government," he added.
Ahmed said the caretaker government should be the first to submit to scrutiny.
"Moslem candidates must have a basic knowledge of Islam... should abide by basic injuctions of Islam and should be trustworthy," he said. "But we demand that elections should not be unduly delayed."
He said his party's 80-member central shura (council) would meet on Wednesday and Thursday in Lahore, capital of the Punjab provinc to discuss future strategy.
Leghari sacked Bhutto, 43, accusing her government of corruption and nepotism. He named veteran politician Meraj Khalid as caretaker prime minister.
